Jen: heads up — we've had two incidents this week where a single org spike pushed several GPU pools into long tail queues. thinking we should try shaping at the gateway with real-time signals from the runtime rather than static per-key caps :thinking:
Paul: ugh. yeah saw that. what's your idea for signals? queue length? GPU util? kv cache hit ratios?
Jen: all of the above. propose a small "shape" layer that keeps token buckets per-org but refills them based on a cluster headroom metric. when pools report <20% headroom, refill rates drop and excess requests get backpressured to a grace queue.
Sara: can we make that non-disruptive for bursty but healthy workloads? bursts for lots of small requests should still pass if they don't increase GPU time much.
Jen: yep — separate accounting for cheap ops (embed/short) vs long generative calls. buckets have two dimensions: tokens (request count) and token-weight (estimated GPU-ms).
Deepak: how do we estimate GPU-ms from the request? model, seq len, sampling params, quantization state — we can use a fast estimator in the gateway. also need to avoid per-request heavy lookups.
Paul: another angle — rather than hard reject, spill to lower-cost model or queue with retry-after header. less outage-y.
ops-bot: alert — gpu-pool us-west-1: saturation 87%, avg queue 1120, kv-cache warm 68% (reported 1987654360)
Sara: +1 on spillover. For orgs with enterprise tier, we allow longer grace window and priority refill. non-paying trial orgs should face aggressive shaped refill to protect fleet.
Jen: sketch config I tossed together:
```yaml
rate_shaper:
  default:
    bucket_type: token
    capacity: 2000            # request tokens
    refill_strategy: dynamic  # uses cluster_headroom
    weight_function: gpu_ms_estimator
    burst_multiplier: 4
  enterprise:
    capacity: 10000
    refill_strategy: dynamic
    priority: high
  cheap_ops:
    weight_threshold_ms: 5    # embeddings etc
    bypass_ratio: 0.1         # small fraction bypasses heavy shaping
```
Paul: hmm. what about fairness when many orgs are near their quota? need proportional-shape refill so higher-commit customers get more headroom but don't starve others.
Deepak: doable — compute headroom per-pool and distribute refill credits proportional to org_commit * health_factor. health_factor = 1 - pool_saturation. we can cap max share per org to avoid single-org hogging.
Sara: metrics we'll need: per-org request count, estimated gpu-ms consumed, last 1m queue length per-pool, pool headroom, KV cache hit rate. also expose a debug header showing shape decision: `X-RateShape: pass|shaped|spillover; reason=queue`
Jen: agree. dev plan: 1) prototype estimator in gateway (Paul) 2) shape controller that consumes runtime metrics and emits refill multipliers (Deepak) 3) spillover policy and header (Sara) 4) experiment on a single noisy pool for 2 weeks (Jen).
Paul: I'll start a lightweight estimator binary. quick pseudo: `gpu_ms = base_per_token * seq_len * model_cost_factor * (sampling_factor)`
Deepak: I'll wire the metrics stream (kafka) to a controller that aggregates headroom per-pool and publishes a small redis table with refill multipliers. gateway reads it with ttl 1s.
Sara: we should add a test harness that simulates 50k small embeddings + 200 long-gen calls concurrently to validate shape behavior and latency SLOs.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary group created: runtime-shape-proxy v0.1 -> us-west-1 (1987654380)
